hero.lede: 134 km from Ljubljana to the Adriatic, past bike-friendly stays, coffee stops and restaurants, with chargers and bike services along the way.

body.intro: Ljubljana to Trieste crosses three landscapes in a day: the green edge of the capital, the stone villages of the Karst and the Adriatic coast. Zyflow lines up the bike-friendly places in between, so the ride is as much about where you stop as how far you go.

sections.title: Leaving Ljubljana
sections.body: Roll out past Vrhnika on quiet roads. The first coffee stop comes early, and it is worth it: the climb onto the plateau starts soon after. Zyflow shows your expected battery along the whole route, so you can pace the start instead of guessing.

sections.title: Karst villages & stops
sections.body: Between Postojna and Divača the road rises and falls through stone villages, with family restaurants and guesthouses that welcome bikes. Charging and water sit right where the hardest sections begin.
bullets: See road closures and roadworks on the route before you leave

sections.title: Descent to the Adriatic
sections.body: After Sežana the plateau ends and the road drops toward the Gulf of Trieste. Finish with a coffee by the sea, or stay the night and ride back tomorrow.

article.title: why e-bike charging at hospitality stops matters
article.lede: A charger at a café or guesthouse can decide how far a ride goes. Here’s why, and how to find one.

body.p1: There’s a particular kind of confidence you only get when you know where the next charger is. If a stop isn’t visible online, many riders never find it, and longer rides shrink to whatever feels safe to guess.
body.p2: Many cafés, restaurants and guesthouses already let riders charge an e-bike. Few of them say so anywhere a rider would look. So the charger exists, but for planning it might as well not.
body.p3: Before a longer ride, check where chargers sit relative to the hardest climbs. It takes a few minutes and changes what the whole day can look like.
body.h2: plan for the climb, not the café
body.p4: Battery drain is not even. A flat stretch costs little, while a long climb, a headwind or a cold morning can cost a lot. Plan for the load you will put on the battery, not the easy kilometres you remember.
body.li1: Range check. Set your e-bike range honestly, including the assist level you actually use
body.li2: Climb window. See where the hardest climbs sit between known chargers
body.li3: Weather and wind. Headwinds and cold can reshape the same route overnight
body.p5: Zyflow builds these into the battery plan and shows chargers along the route, so you’re not inventing stops mid-climb.
body.h3: start with the right day ride
body.p6: Not all routes are created equal. A rolling countryside day is where almost every rider should start. The rhythm is predictable, and you have time to learn how your battery behaves without the mountains making decisions for you.
body.quote: “If a charger isn’t visible online, many riders never find it. And longer rides shrink to whatever feels safe to guess.”
body.p7: Bigger alpine days are a different discipline. They are exhilarating, but they reward planning. Start with a rolling day ride, learn how your battery behaves, then go further. And if you run a café or guesthouse with a socket to spare, tell us. Riders are looking for you.

hero.storyTitle: Great places to stop are everywhere. Most maps just don’t show them.
hero.storyBody: We’re Jakob and Tanja, the team behind Zyflow, made by HERKO d.o.o. in Slovenia. Zyflow helps cyclists and e-bike riders find bike-friendly stays, coffee stops, restaurants and chargers, and ride between them feeling safe. Today it is live on iOS and Android in 8 countries, with 7,400+ chargers mapped and data from partners like Open Data Hub. Next: more countries, more places, and more ways to keep riders safe.

items.body: Zyflow is here so you can say yes to the detour. Every place shows whether your bike is welcome, so the next stop is a choice, not a gamble.
Road closures, bike theft by area and chargers along the way. We show what we know, so you can decide before you ride.
We only promise what the app does today. When something is still being built, we say so, and we listen when riders tell us what to fix next.
Zyflow is free on iOS and Android, for every rider and every bike. Start with one stop, then go further.
